objectives.text: Tell a push from a pull and say what each does to an object, and explain how friction slows a sliding object down
successCriteria: I can say a push moves something away from you and a pull brings it closer
I can explain that friction is the rubbing force between the block and the rough surface and that it pushes back against the slide and slows the block down
assessmentPoints: Push and pull answers in the opening activity
Responses when the friction arrow is followed in the second activity

objectives.text: State what happens when opposite poles and when like poles face each other, and name the metal a magnet reliably pulls while explaining why not every metal is pulled
successCriteria: I can say opposite poles attract and snap together, and like poles repel and push each other apart
I can name iron as the metal a magnet reliably pulls and say a magnet only pulls iron and a few metals, ignoring most other metals
assessmentPoints: Pole predictions in the third activity
Worksheet and exit ticket answers in the closing practice

activities.title: Push and pull: which force moves the box?

differentiation.support: Provide the two magnets with their N and S pole labels facing the class so learners can read the poles before predicting attract or repel.

activities.title: Like poles repel and the metal trap

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why a shiny metal object must be tested one by one instead of being assumed magnetic.
